decisionKinds.meaning: The grammar contract is exactly one an existing owner already parses. The carrier delegates the region to that owner unchanged, through the embedded-language row (CAT0 T05). No copy, no mode flag in the owner.
requires: the owner's pinned corpus covers the region's exact grammar contract
the owner adds no branch naming the consuming carrier or profile

decisionKinds.meaning: An owner-declared dialect hook of an existing parser that keeps the owner's lossless tree model (SCSS/Less over CSS, SQL dialects, JSON5 over JSON, Liquid dialect profiles). The dialect is a typed owner-local table, never a framework branch.
requires: the hook is declared by the owner and named by a dialect identity that enters the syntax profile
a construct gated by one dialect never parses under another dialect identity
the owner's base corpus still passes unchanged

decisionKinds.meaning: Copy the closest proven parser into a new owner, remove the source's carrier assumptions and specialise. The fork has no dependency back to its source and re-proves its own corpus and recovery.
requires: no manifest or module edge from the fork to its source
the source's recovery semantics are re-proven on the fork's own corpus, never inherited by assertion

decisionKinds.meaning: A dedicated in-house parser for a grammar no existing owner covers and no proven parser is close enough to fork.
requires: the evidence that the closest parser failed the pinned grammar/recovery corpus, or that no candidate exists

decisionKinds.meaning: A semantic (framework) profile over canonical syntax owners: an overlay on JS/TS/JSX/TSX (React, Solid, Preact, Qwik, Stencil) or an attachment on HTML attributes or tagged templates (Lit, Alpine, htmx, Stimulus). It registers no frontend and declares no grammar; its value languages are codecs (EMB0) or Reuse rows.
requires: no CarrierFrontend registration and no grammar config for the profile
value codecs are profile-owned results over shared codec primitives (EMB0I-AC1)

contracts.name: ParserDecision
contracts.rule: Every exact grammar contract a carrier, region or document language needs has exactly one ParserDecision. Fields: grammar contract (grammar name and exact specification edition or release), CarrierProfileId (VID0 I03) of the carrier or embedded carrier it serves, decision kind (DK1-DK5), owner (parser home, H.. or an existing route G..), ParserId, ParserGrammarEpoch, lineage, license, oracle corpus, recovery class, budget class, delegations (region role to embedded grammar contract via CAT0 T05) and the evidence that selected the kind. The decision is data on the carrier row and the vertical manifest; it is not implementation support and not a compiler commitment.
contracts.home: manifest parser section (VIM0 schema, VIM1 compiler) rendered onto the CAT0 T01 carrier row

contracts.name: Ownership key
contracts.rule: Parser ownership is keyed by (CarrierProfileId, ParserGrammarEpoch). One exact grammar contract has one owner. A family name, a FrameworkProfileId, an adapter spelling, a file extension or 'HTML-like' is never an ownership, selection or cache key (VID0 R03, R15; CAT0 CR10). Selection reads the typed CarrierProfileId from the catalog or the DemandPlan; an unresolved framework name selects nothing and yields the typed unsupported outcome.

contracts.name: Reuse equality and cache keys
contracts.rule: Two parses are interchangeable only when (ContentId, CarrierProfileId, ParserId, ParserGrammarEpoch, SyntaxProfileId) are equal; SyntaxProfileId carries the normalised parse options and dialect identity. A content hash alone, or a content hash plus path, never admits reuse. Syntax artifacts never key on a semantic profile (VID0 R15). Grammar-epoch, dialect or option change misses exactly the affected carrier's artifacts. A cancelled, stale or partial parse is never admitted as complete or warmed.

contracts.name: Lineage, license and corpus record
contracts.rule: A ForkAndSpecialize or NewParser decision records: source owner and its grammar epoch (for a fork of an in-repository parser, its module path plus the landing title and ISO date of the source state), upstream specification or project by name and released version, SPDX license of any adapted upstream material, and the oracle corpus by name, released version and checked-in path with a content digest. Commit SHAs, hashes or URLs are never lineage evidence. Third-party implementations are oracles only; none is a product parser dependency.

contracts.name: Lossless recovery, error, fuzz and budget obligations
contracts.rule: Every owned parser is lossless (concatenating tokens and trivia reproduces the input bytes exactly), error-tolerant (always a tree plus located typed diagnostics, never a panic or abort on any input), with exact UTF-8 spans (ENC0). Recovery semantics belong to the owning grammar and are proven on its own malformed corpus; sharing recovery between parsers requires that proof for each. Each parser declares bounded nesting with a typed depth diagnostic, linear-time scanning per input byte, and its expansion budgets (for example XML entities). Fuzzing asserts no panic, termination and the round trip. Budgets bind to the owning performance methodology; wall-clock evidence is a bench-m3 evidence run and never gates.

contracts.name: Evidence-gated HTML-family extraction
contracts.rule: The neutral HTML parser is a ForkAndSpecialize of the Vue tokenizer lineage into its own home (HWC1). No shared 'HTML family' parser, recovery mode or cache key exists. A carrier with HTML-shaped content (Astro, Marko, Glimmer, Angular templates) chooses NewParser or ForkAndSpecialize over the neutral HTML parser in its P0 lock. Extracting a shared tokenizer from several forks is reserved: it is admitted only by a later decision that shows each consumer's pinned corpus and recovery corpus pass unchanged through the extracted owner, and it never adds a carrier branch to the neutral parser.

contracts.name: Retained-snapshot boundary
contracts.rule: Parser ownership preserves the engine's retained-snapshot boundary: verter_semantic discovers, verter_semantic_source lowers demanded bodies through the scheduler-retained parse snapshot, verter_session_query carries owned data. Session and scheduler keep acquisition and execution. No second parse or lowering cache, no engine-to-parser dependency, parse once per parse key, zero eager declaration bodies.

contracts.name: Parser homes and layer placement
contracts.rule: A parser lives in (a) a dedicated verter_<grammar>_syntax crate, the default, or (b) a dialect module of the existing owner whose lossless tree model it shares. It never lives in a crate of the parser-free closure (verter_identity, verter_span, verter_language, verter_session_query, verter_type_engine, verter_type_expr, verter_execution), never in a compiler-backend module (UAK1 LC), and a neutral grammar never lives in a vertical crate. Vertical carrier grammars are UAK1 L3; neutral grammars (HTML, Pug, CSS dialects, document languages, regex) are neutral syntax owners like verter_css_syntax. A parser crate may depend on verter_language for the neutral parse-artifact DTOs, on verter_span, and on the neutral syntax owners its Reuse rows name; it depends on no semantic profile and on no compiler backend.

contracts.name: Admission policy
contracts.rule: OXC is the only JS/TS/JSX/TSX parser and is reached only through the verter_parser::oxc_parse choke point. Every other product parser is in-house, lossless and error-tolerant with exact spans. No third-party parser crate is admitted as a product parser; the toml crate is internal config reading only until TOMLX removes it. OXC's parse_regular_expression option stays off and oxc_regular_expression is never a direct dependency; ECMAScript regex is verter_regex's (RGX1). Official conformance suites are checked in as oracles. A formatter or linter contains no parser.

findings.finding: The retained OXC parse snapshot is keyed by content only: SnapshotKey {canonical, whole_hash, parse_env_hash} carries no parser identity, grammar epoch or SourceType, and a warm hit ignores the requested SourceType. No defect is reproduced; PD03 forbids the shape. No PAR0 descendant charters the engine snapshot key.

Two grammar-version notions: CarrierParserGrammarVersion enters grammar_fingerprint only, while ParseKey uses per-domain CompatibilityEpoch constants. PD03 needs one ParserGrammarEpoch in the parse key.
LSO1C keys RecoverySnapshot by FrameworkProfileId. A recovery snapshot is a syntax artifact; VID0 R15 and PD03 key it by CarrierProfileId, ParserId and ParserGrammarEpoch.

OXC SourceType for a script region is chosen by at least ten independent mappings that disagree on defaults (G02). The target is one neutral mapping from the region's embedded CarrierProfileId (CAT0 T05) to the OXC SourceType.
Four in-house JSONC comment strippers feed serde_json for tsconfig, project config and editor config (G12). No PAR0 descendant charters their cutover onto CL29.
JSDoc tags are scanned by three hand-written scanners (verter_semantic jsdoc and function_program_hash, verter_compiler tsc::script) beside the one payload parser.

REG0 pre-registers crates/verter_language/src/carriers/<carrier> as parser homes 'when PAR0 places them in verter_language'. PAR0 does not: verter_language is in the parser-free closure (verter_session_query and verter_type_engine depend on it), so REG0 creates H01-H07 instead. LIQ1 and ERB1 likewise add central CarrierGrammarConfig arms and a private CST in verter_language parse_artifact.rs; both move to owner-local rows (CAT0 CAT-F03) and their homes.
TOMLX lists four toml manifests; there are five. verter_source_policy_gate also declares toml as a dev-dependency, and cargo tree includes dev edges, so TOMLX-AC1 needs it too.
HWC1's production surfaces name crates/verter_language/src for the neutral HTML parser and DIAL1's conflict domain names crates/verter_parser for Pug. PD08 places them in H08 and H09.
